name: Cutouts
description_preview:
Cutouts is The Smile’s third studio album, featuring tracks written and performed live during the sessions and tours for their previous albums, A Light for Attracting Attention (2022) and Wall of Eyes (2024), but not included in those releases.

This album follows just months after Wall of Eyes, which came out in January. The first single from Cutouts, “Don’t Get Me Started” was released digitally and as a limited edition vinyl with “The Slip” as the B-side in select indie stores.

In an interview promoting Wall of Eyes, Thom Yorke noted, “The ones that we haven’t released, we either just haven’t recorded yet or we’re working on,” while Tom Skinner added, “There are more songs but those eight just sort of fit together. It wasn’t a really conscious thing; they just all seemed to work together somehow. Sam [Petts-Davies] helped us to see that,” referring to the tracks now featured on Cutouts.

On August 23, 2024, The Smile started teasing the album by posting various coded messages on their social media, including Caesar ciphers, Playfair ciphers, Polybius ciphers, Hexahue alphabet, Solfa ciphers, Base64 encoding, Pigpen ciphers, and even an IBM 80-column punched card. Fans were challenged to decipher these codes, which revealed the names and positions of the album’s tracks. Cutouts was officially announced on August 28, 2024, along with the release of the songs “Foreign Spies” and “Zero Sum”.

body.plain:
As with their previous albums A Light for Attracting Attention (2022) and Wall of Eyes (2024), the cover of Cutouts also features artwork by Thom Yorke and Stanley Donwood. This painting is called “Two Moons” and is part of the duo’s exhibition at London’s TIN MAN ART, titled “The Crow Flies,” This collection emerged from creative sessions that coincided with the recording of their earlier albums, adding a visual dimension to their musical exploration.



 Two Moons (2023) by Stanley Donwood & Thom Yorke

body.plain: The back cover of Cutouts is the painting “Let Us Raise Our Glasses To What We Don’t Deserve”, painted in 2023 during the recording sessions for Wall of Eyes. In fact, the title of the painting is a line from the song “Wall of Eyes” and was also written in the newspaper edition of Radiohead’s 2011 album The King of Limbs.
